Hi James — great questions, thanks for consolidating. Looping in Vanessa (marketplace ops) and Ben (go-to-market) who will help with the listing language and co-sell script. Answers inline below and a suggested approach for the product page.

- AMI visibility: For AWS Marketplace we typically publish a private AMI tied to the offering so customers subscribe via the listing and the AMI is distributed by AWS. Public AMIs are possible but we avoid them for managed offerings.
- Size: highlight the expected base AMI footprint (we recommend quoting ~12–20GB) and call out optional data volumes. Keep the first line short — customers care about install time not exact bytes.
- Billing line: yes — we can use a short note: "Usage-based inference pricing via Redwood; Dedicated/Reserved capacity options available for enterprise buyers." (Ben: please refine).
- Co-sell blurb: Redwood prefers this approved line for marketplace pages: "Partner-backed deployment with joint sales support — contact your Redwood account team for co-sell enablement." (Vanessa: confirm if this needs legal review).

Suggested product page structure (short copy only):
• One-liner: "High-performance LLM inference as a managed AMI — predictable throughput and enterprise controls."
• 2–3 bullet benefits: low-latency inference, dedicated pools, auditable logs
• Installation note: brief AMI footprint + subscription steps
• Pricing snippet: one sentence as above + link to pricing tiers
• Co-sell CTA: "Request joint enablement" (link to playbook / contact form)

I attached a cleaned-up blurb and a quick co-sell outreach script for SDRs. If that looks good I can send the assets to our AWS listing contact once we confirm the final one-liner.

Thanks — Tessa
Tessa Morgan
Head of Partnerships, Redwood Inference
